[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Paired t-test: To compare means of strength tests before and after the transition.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. ANOVA: To determine significant differences in strength development between players who transitioned to elite level and those who remained in the academy.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Regression analysis: To determine the relationship between strength development and time.

[USER] Asked for a usable approach to investigate development with six measurements spread between before and after transition.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended using repeated-measures ANOVA to investigate strength development over time.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Explained that repeated-measures ANOVA is suitable for comparing means across multiple time points in a within-subjects design.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested using a linear mixed-effects model as an alternative to account for repeated measures and individual differences.  
[USER] Requested R code in a tidyverse style for an ANOVA analysis with a dataframe called: both_debuttest3_selecttest.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Provided R code for conducting a repeated-measures ANOVA:  
```r
library(tidyverse)

# Load the data
both_debuttest3_selecttest <- read.csv("both_debuttest3_selecttest.csv")

# Convert the data to a tidy format
both_debuttest3_selecttest_tidy <- both_debuttest3_selecttest %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(Player, Time),
               names_to = "Test",
               values_to = "Strength")

# Perform the repeated-measures ANOVA
aov_results <- aov(Strength ~ Time*Test + Error(Player/Test), data = both_debuttest3_selecttest_tidy)

# Print the ANOVA table
summary(aov_results)
```
